Introduction to Forensic Science: Forensic science
The application of science to matters of law
Criminalistics
The branch analysing physical evidence from crime scenes
Locard's exchange principle
Every contact leaves a trace between two objects
Physical evidence
Any object that can connect a person to a crime
Direct evidence
Evidence that proves a fact without inference, such as an eyewitness
Circumstantial evidence
Evidence requiring an inference to connect it to a conclusion
Class characteristic
A trait shared by a group of similar objects
Individual characteristic
A trait traceable to one single source
Expert witness
A qualified specialist permitted to give opinion testimony
Frye standard
The rule that a technique must be generally accepted in its field
Daubert standard
The modern rule making judges gatekeepers of scientific reliability
Forensic laboratory units
Divisions such as biology, chemistry, firearms, and documents
Medical examiner
A physician who investigates cause and manner of death
Crime Scene Investigation: Crime scene
The location where a crime occurred and evidence may remain
Securing the scene
Restricting access to prevent contamination or loss
Primary versus secondary scene
The location of the crime versus a related location
Chain of custody
The documented record of everyone who handled evidence
Contamination
The unwanted introduction of outside material to evidence
Search pattern
A systematic method such as spiral, grid, or zone
Grid search
Overlapping parallel sweeps in two directions
Evidence log
The written record of every item collected
Sketching a scene
Producing a scaled diagram showing evidence positions
Photographic documentation
Overall, midrange, and close-up images with a scale
Packaging evidence
Using paper or breathable containers to prevent mould on biological items
Bindle
A folded paper packet used for trace evidence
Reconstruction
Determining the sequence of events from the physical evidence
Buccal swab
A reference DNA sample taken from the inside of a cheek
Fingerprint Analysis: Fingerprint
The reproduction of friction ridge patterns from the fingertip
Principles of fingerprints
They are unique, permanent, and classifiable
Loop pattern
The most common pattern, with ridges entering and exiting the same side
Whorl pattern
A circular or spiral ridge pattern
Arch pattern
The least common pattern, with ridges rising and falling
Minutiae
Ridge details such as bifurcations and endings used for identification
Ridge ending
A point where a friction ridge stops
Bifurcation
A point where one ridge splits into two
Latent print
An invisible print left by natural skin secretions
Patent print
A visible print left in a substance such as blood or paint
Plastic print
A three-dimensional impression left in a soft material
Dusting with powder
Developing latent prints on smooth nonporous surfaces
Ninhydrin
A chemical developing prints on porous surfaces by reacting with amino acids
Cyanoacrylate fuming
Superglue vapour that adheres to and reveals latent prints
AFIS
The automated database that searches fingerprints against stored records
Trace Evidence: Hair and Fiber: Trace evidence
Small quantities of material transferred between people or objects
Hair shaft
The visible portion of a hair, composed of cuticle, cortex, and medulla
Cuticle
The overlapping outer scales of a hair
Cortex
The hair layer containing pigment granules
Medulla
The central canal of a hair, whose pattern helps identify species
Medullary index
The medulla diameter relative to the whole hair diameter
Anagen phase
The active growth stage, when a hair has a follicular tag with DNA
Telogen phase
The resting stage, when hair sheds without root material
Hair as class evidence
Microscopic comparison narrows the source but rarely identifies one person
Natural fiber
A fibre from a plant or animal, such as cotton or wool
Synthetic fiber
A manufactured fibre such as polyester or nylon
Fiber cross-section
The shape of a fibre, which can indicate its manufacturer
Birefringence
The difference in refractive indices used to identify fibres
Microspectrophotometry
Comparing fibre colour by measuring absorbed wavelengths
Blood and Bloodstain Patterns: Presumptive test
A screening test indicating a substance may be blood
Kastle-Meyer test
A phenolphthalein test that turns pink in the presence of blood
Luminol
A chemical that glows where blood is present, even after cleaning
Confirmatory test
A test establishing that a stain definitely is human blood
Blood typing
Classifying blood into A, B, AB, and O groups by antigens
Antigen
A surface marker on a red blood cell that determines type
Rh factor
An additional antigen making a blood type positive or negative
Bloodstain pattern analysis
Interpreting stain shape and distribution to reconstruct events
Passive drop
A stain formed by gravity alone, typically circular
Impact spatter
Small stains created when a force strikes a blood source
Cast-off pattern
Blood flung from a moving object such as a swung weapon
Arterial spurt
A pattern produced by pressurised blood from a severed artery
Transfer stain
A pattern left when a bloody object contacts a clean surface
Void pattern
An empty area showing something blocked the spatter
Angle of impact
Calculated from a stain's width-to-length ratio
Area of convergence
The two-dimensional point from which spatter originated
DNA Analysis: DNA
The molecule carrying genetic instructions, unique except in identical twins
Nuclear DNA
DNA from the cell nucleus, inherited from both parents
Mitochondrial DNA
DNA inherited only from the mother, useful for degraded samples
Short tandem repeat
A short DNA sequence repeated a variable number of times
CODIS
The national DNA database used to compare offender and case profiles
Polymerase chain reaction
A technique amplifying tiny amounts of DNA
Electrophoresis
Separating DNA fragments by size using an electric field
DNA profile
The set of STR values that identifies an individual
Touch DNA
Trace genetic material left by skin cells on a surface
Reference sample
A known sample used for comparison against evidence
Exclusion
A result proving a suspect could not be the source
Random match probability
The chance an unrelated person shares the same profile
Degraded sample
DNA broken down by heat, moisture, or time
Y-STR analysis
Testing the Y chromosome to isolate male contributors in a mixture
Toxicology and Drugs: Forensic toxicology
The study of drugs and poisons in body fluids and tissues
Controlled substance
A drug whose manufacture and possession are regulated by law
Drug schedules
Legal classifications ranked by abuse potential and medical use
Depressant
A drug that slows central nervous system activity
Stimulant
A drug that increases alertness and heart rate
Narcotic analgesic
An opioid drug relieving pain and causing dependence
Hallucinogen
A drug that alters perception and sensory experience
Screening test for drugs
A rapid colour or immunoassay test suggesting a drug class
Gas chromatography
A technique separating components of a mixture
Mass spectrometry
A technique identifying compounds by their fragmentation pattern
GC-MS
The combined gold-standard method for drug identification
Blood alcohol concentration
The percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream
Breathalyzer
A device estimating blood alcohol from breath
Half-life of a drug
The time for the body to eliminate half a dose
Postmortem redistribution
Drug concentrations shifting after death, complicating interpretation
Firearms and Toolmarks: Ballistics
The study of projectile motion and firearm evidence
Rifling
The spiral grooves cut inside a barrel to spin a bullet
Lands and grooves
The raised and cut portions of rifling that mark a bullet
Caliber
The diameter of a bullet or the bore of a firearm
Gauge
A shotgun size measure, where a smaller number means a larger bore
Striations
The fine parallel scratches a barrel leaves on a bullet
Breech face marks
Impressions left on a cartridge case by the rear of the chamber
Firing pin impression
The dent left on a primer when a round is fired
Comparison microscope
An instrument viewing two samples side by side in one field
NIBIN
The national database comparing ballistic evidence across cases
Gunshot residue
Particles of lead, barium, and antimony deposited when firing
Distance determination
Estimating firing range from residue spread around a wound
Toolmark
An impression or scratch left by a tool on a softer surface
Serial number restoration
Chemically revealing a filed-off identifying number
Document and Handwriting Analysis: Questioned document
Any document whose authenticity or authorship is in dispute
Exemplar
A known writing sample used for comparison
Requested exemplar
A sample written on demand, which a suspect may disguise
Collected exemplar
A sample from everyday writing done before the investigation
Individual writing characteristic
A personal habit such as letter slant or spacing
Class writing characteristic
A trait taught by a writing system shared by many
Line quality
The smoothness or hesitation visible in a stroke
Pen lift
A break in a stroke that can suggest tracing or forgery
Simulated forgery
A signature copied by imitating a genuine model
Traced forgery
A signature produced by following an original underneath
Indented writing
Impressions left on a lower page, revealed with an ESDA
Ink analysis
Comparing inks by chromatography or spectral response
Watermark
A design in paper used to identify the manufacturer
Counterfeit detection
Examining security features such as microprinting and threads
Forensic Anthropology: The examination of skeletal remains for legal purposes
The most reliable skeletal indicator of biological sex
Using growth plate fusion and dental development
The closing of growth plates, which follows a predictable timeline
Calculating height from long bone length using regression formulas
An injury showing healing, so it occurred before death
An injury occurring at or near the time of death
Breakage occurring after death, with dry fracture characteristics
Injury from a wide impact causing radiating fractures
Injury from a cutting or stabbing implement
Rebuilding likely appearance from skull structure
The study of what happens to remains after death
Entomology and Time of Death: Forensic entomology
Using insect evidence to estimate time since death
Postmortem interval
The elapsed time between death and discovery
Algor mortis
The cooling of the body after death
Livor mortis
The pooling of blood producing skin discolouration
Rigor mortis
The stiffening of muscles that peaks then passes
Fixed lividity
Discolouration that no longer blanches, indicating hours have passed
Blowfly life cycle
Egg, three larval instars, pupa, and adult
First colonizer
The blowfly, which typically arrives within minutes to hours
Instar
A developmental stage between larval moults
Accumulated degree hours
Heat units used to estimate insect development time
Effect of temperature on decomposition
Warmth accelerates both insect growth and decay
Stages of decomposition
Fresh, bloat, active decay, advanced decay, and dry remains
Stomach contents
Digestive state used to estimate time since the last meal
Vitreous humor potassium
Eye fluid chemistry that rises predictably after death
Courtroom Testimony and Ethics: Testimony
Sworn statements given by a witness in court
Direct examination
Questioning by the attorney who called the witness
Cross-examination
Questioning by the opposing attorney to test credibility
Voir dire of an expert
Questioning to establish a witness's qualifications
Opinion testimony
Conclusions an expert may state that a lay witness may not
Report writing
Documenting methods and findings clearly enough for others to review
Objectivity
Following the evidence rather than the desired outcome
Confirmation bias
Interpreting evidence to support a preexisting belief
Contextual bias
Being influenced by case information irrelevant to the analysis
Peer review in forensics
Independent checking of an analyst's conclusions
Proficiency testing
Regular blind testing that verifies an analyst's accuracy
Laboratory accreditation
Formal certification that a lab meets quality standards
Exculpatory evidence
Evidence favouring the defendant, which must be disclosed
Burden of proof
The prosecution's obligation to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt
Wrongful conviction
A conviction later shown to be mistaken, often revealed by DNA
